players.product: NovaLT and Frame 5 gas turbines plus Brush generators for behind-the-meter data-center power (Chart Industries thermal management added July 2026)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 headline results (CEO/CFO): adjusted EBITDA totaled $1.16 billion, above the guidance range, up 12% year-over-year; adjusted EBITDA margin rose 140 basis points to 17.6%; adjusted EPS $0.58, up 13%; total company orders $8.2 billion; free cash flow $210 million (Q1 seasonally weakest, also hit by delayed customer payments). Results absorbed Middle East conflict disruption, the PSI divestiture and the SPC joint venture.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted EBITDA $1.16 billion (17.6% margin); adjusted EPS $0.58; orders $8.2 billion; free cash flow $210 million

quarterly_data.signal: IET segment: record orders of $4.9 billion (third straight quarter above $4 billion), including $1.4 billion of Power Systems orders; book-to-bill 1.5x; record IET RPO of $33.1 billion; last-4-quarter IET orders $16.6 billion, up 25%. IET revenue $3.35 billion (+14% YoY, high end of guidance) led by Gas Tech Services working down the overdue aeroderivative backlog; IET EBITDA $678 million (+35%), margin 20.2% (+310 bps) on favorable backlog pricing, project closeout and productivity.
quarterly_data.figure: IET orders $4.9 billion; Power Systems orders $1.4 billion; IET RPO $33.1 billion; IET revenue $3.35 billion; IET EBITDA $678 million (20.2%)

quarterly_data.signal: Data-center power award: Baker Hughes converted a prior slot reservation agreement into an integrated solution award for a critical infrastructure project in North America, including NovaLT16 gas turbines, BRUSH Power Generation electric generators, gears and long-term aftermarket services, 'delivering up to 1 gigawatt of reliable power to support growing energy demand from data centers' (customer not named). Separately, a contract to provide 25 BRUSH Power Generation generators to Boom Supersonic which, paired with Boom's gas turbines, is expected to deliver 1.21 gigawatts of generator capacity for data centers.
quarterly_data.figure: up to 1 gigawatt NovaLT16 + BRUSH award; 25 BRUSH generators (1.21 gigawatts) for Boom Supersonic

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: CEO said 'we're effectively sold out of NovaLTs through 2028 and the tightness we're seeing across the broader turbine market is well understood'; capacity is being doubled, inbound NovaLT demand remains strong and opportunities are prioritized for long-term partners with financing and offtake firmly in place; expansion beyond the current doubling plan would require a disciplined supply-demand and return assessment. Frame 5 gas turbines have available capacity in '27 and '28; capacity was added to BRUSH generator and synchronous condenser lines, and an aftermarket NovaLT facility was inaugurated in Italy.
quarterly_data.figure: NovaLT effectively sold out through 2028; Frame 5 capacity available in '27 and '28

quarterly_data.signal: Power demand framing: CEO said power demand is projected to double by 2040, driven by data center and AI compute among other factors; grid constraints (particularly in the US) are driving a fundamental shift to behind-the-meter power, which customers increasingly deploy as long-term baseload infrastructure rather than short-term bridge solutions; Baker Hughes sees the behind-the-meter market reaching $60 billion by 2030, led by data centers. Q1 Power Systems orders of $1.4 billion were almost 30% of total IET orders; Cordant power-related orders doubled year-over-year after power orders rose more than 80% in 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: behind-the-meter market $60 billion by 2030; Power Systems almost 30% of IET orders

quarterly_data.signal: Energy management and grid: announced a collaboration with Google Cloud to develop AI-enabled power optimization and sustainability solutions for data center applications; received a second engineering/design contract for Hydrostor's compressed air energy storage system, with up to 1.4 gigawatts of potential equipment orders. In grid stability (not data-center related), Baker Hughes 'secured a contract with Hitachi Energy to design, manufacture, install and commission 4 synchronous condensers' for 2 energy substations in Australia. New energy orders were $1.4 billion in Q1 (including the 1 gigawatt data center order), supporting the $2.4 billion to $2.6 billion 2026 target.
quarterly_data.figure: new energy orders $1.4 billion; 2026 target $2.4 billion to $2.6 billion; Hydrostor up to 1.4 gigawatts potential

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance (CFO, midpoints, assuming the Middle East situation lasts through end of June): Q2 company revenue $6.5 billion and adjusted EBITDA $1.13 billion; Q2 IET EBITDA $670 million with IET revenue flat sequentially; Q2 OFSE EBITDA $540 million on revenue of $3.2 billion. Full-year company revenue/EBITDA ranges maintained (slightly below midpoint); IET orders at least the $14.5 billion midpoint; IET EBITDA at least the $2.7 billion midpoint; OFSE at the low end of EBITDA range, $2.325 billion, if the conflict ends by June. CEO increasingly confident the Horizon 2 IET order target will exceed $40 billion (by 2028).
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $6.5 billion, adjusted EBITDA $1.13 billion; FY IET orders at least $14.5 billion; FY IET EBITDA at least $2.7 billion; Horizon 2 IET orders to exceed $40 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Chart Industries acquisition (pre-close): closing then expected in the second quarter pending regulatory reviews; integration office organized into 17 work streams has identified more than 250 synergy opportunities, confident in the full $325 million cost synergy target. March debt issuance of $6.5 billion in US bonds and EUR 3 billion in European bonds to fund the closing; cash position $14.8 billion. Portfolio actions (PSI, SPC JV, Waygate sale, HMH IPO) expected to generate approximately $3 billion of gross proceeds in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: $325 million cost synergies; more than 250 synergy opportunities; $6.5 billion US bonds + EUR 3 billion
